text_blocks.snippet: In Utah, a full roof replacement typically costs [Highlight start] between $8,000 and $17,000 [Highlight end] for a standard asphalt shingle roof on an average-sized home, though larger homes, steep pitches, or premium materials can push costs to $20,000–$36,000+.

list.snippet: Asphalt shingles: About $4.50–$8.25 per sq. ft. (roughly $9,000–$16,500 for a 2,000 sq. ft. roof). Most users on Reddit agree that recent asphalt shingle replacements for 1,700–2,000 sq. ft. footprints around Salt Lake City generally land around $12,000–$17,000.
Designer shingles: About $9.00–$18.00 per sq. ft. (roughly $18,000–$36,000 for a 2,000 sq. ft. roof).
Metal roofing: About $8.00–$17.00 per sq. ft. (roughly $16,000–$34,000 for a 2,000 sq. ft. roof).

text_blocks.snippet: On Facebook, opinions are mixed on larger Utah roofs (around 2,600 sq. ft.), with reported estimates spanning roughly $5,000 to $23,850 depending on the job scope and materials.
Key Factors That Change Your Quote

list.snippet: Roof size and pitch: Steeper slopes and complex designs (valleys, dormers, multiple stories) require extra labor and safety gear.
Tear-off layers and disposal: Removing multiple layers of old shingles increases labor and landfill weight fees.
Decking and code upgrades: Replacing rotted decking (often around $60–$80 per sheet) or adding ice-and-water shield, ventilation, and flashing to meet local building codes adds to the total.
Utah climate and season: Heavy snow, hail, and high-altitude UV often prompt upgrades to impact-resistant shingles or metal, and peak spring-to-fall demand can affect pricing.
